newsitem.title: COLOMBIA: Colombian stocks end sharply higher for third day.
newsitem.headline: Colombian stocks end sharply higher for third day.

text.p: Colombian stocks ended sharply higher for the third consecutive day as foreign funds and local investors continued to place bets on a drop in interest rates and solid corporate growth.

Medellin's IBOMED general price index rose an impressive 3.36 percent to end at 16,192.49 on an active trading volume of 4.5 billion pesos. Bogota's IBB rose a similar 3.30 percent, closing at 1,036.90 on a volume of more than three billion. "Foreign funds have been buying everything that comes their way," one Bogota-based broker said of the day's bullish performance.
As in the previous two sessions, gainers included brewer Bavaria SA of the Julio Maria Santo Domingo industrial group, which moved up another 4.16 percent to close at 6,750 pesos per share.
But big winners were seen across-the-board in most actively traded shares and included everything from banks and insurance companies to cement and cigarette manufacturers.

Blue-chip Banco Ganadero, the country's biggest comercial bank, saw its ordinary shares rise 3.58 percent in Bogota to close at 318 pesos per share. Banco de Colombia, the country's No. 2 bank, rose 2.83 percent, ending at 435 pesos.

The day's best performers by far were cement maker Cementos del Valle, which jumped 10 percent to end at 4,951 pesos per share, and tobacco company Coltabaco, which ended up 8.57 percent at 3,800 pesos a share.
Both companies belong to the powerful Sindicato Antioqueno conglomerate, which is a favourite among foreign investors.

A widely expected cut in domestic interest rates, which market players say could come as early as next week, could help fuel corporate growth. Brokers say that this is the main reason for the run-up in equities this week. Additionally, they most Colombian shares still look undervalued.
